title: The Adventurer's Name
story: Elder Mira squints at you. "A hero with no name cannot cross the gate. Write it down in Java, and say it aloud."
goal: Create a String variable called name holding "Adventurer", then print Hello, Adventurer! using System.out.println and your variable.
starterCode: // TODO 1: create a String variable called name that holds "Adventurer"

visibleTests.name: declares a String variable called name

hiddenTests.name: prints the variable, not a hard-coded text

hints: A variable is a labelled box. The type String is the box for text.
Declare it like this: String name = "Adventurer"; then join texts with +.
System.out.println("Hello, " + name + "!"); goes on the line after the declaration.
explanation: String name = "Adventurer"; creates a variable: a named place in memory that holds text. System.out.println prints text followed by a new line, and + joins texts together.

commonMistakes.message: Every Java statement ends with a semicolon.
Close! Check capital letters, the comma after Hello and the exclamation mark.
You used print; println also adds the new line the tests expect.
